pointers.sentence: So Django learns the list from each response it stores for a URL and keeps it in the cache under a key made from the URL; a later request reads the list first and builds from it the key of the page, "without building the response object itself", as the docstring says (`django/utils/cache.py:learn_cache_key`).

The module's docstring puts `UpdateCacheMiddleware` first in `MIDDLEWARE` and `FetchFromCacheMiddleware` last, counterintuitive but correct, it says: the update half must run last on the way out, where the chain runs bottom-up, and the fetch half last on the way in (`django/middleware/cache.py`; [Handlers and middleware](../handlers.md#the-chain-is-an-onion)).

So the fetch half makes its key after `LocaleMiddleware` has set the language, and the update half reads the `"Vary"` after `SessionMiddleware`, `GZipMiddleware` and `LocaleMiddleware` have added to it (`docs/topics/cache.txt`).

On a hit, `FetchFromCacheMiddleware.process_request` returns the stored response, and `MiddlewareMixin.__call__` does not call the layer inside it (`django/middleware/__init__.py:MiddlewareMixin.__call__`).

The fetch half sets it true after a miss, and false for a hit or for a method other than `"GET"` and `"HEAD"`; the update half stores only when it is true (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware._should_update_cache`).

With `USE_I18N` on, Accept-Language is left out: a comment says the key already carries the language, and the raw header would store the same content under several keys (ticket 18191) (`django/utils/cache.py:learn_cache_key`).
It reads the list under the header key, returns `None` if there is none, and otherwise builds the page key for the method it is given (`django/utils/cache.py:get_cache_key`).
Both keys hash the URL from `HttpRequest.build_absolute_uri`, host and query string included (`django/utils/cache.py:_generate_cache_header_key`).

The page key also hashes each listed header's value, empty where the request lacks it, as a netstring: its length in bytes, a colon, the bytes and a comma (`django/utils/cache.py:_generate_cache_key`).
Django's tests check that `"EU"` then nothing and nothing then `"EU"` get different keys (`tests/cache/tests.py:CacheUtils.test_learn_cache_key_no_header_collision`).

Then `_i18n_cache_key_suffix` adds, with `USE_I18N`, the language, the request's attribute `LANGUAGE_CODE` where `LocaleMiddleware` has set it and otherwise the active language, and with `USE_TZ` the current time zone's name (`django/utils/cache.py:_i18n_cache_key_suffix`; [Choosing a language: `LocaleMiddleware`](../i18n/choosing.md), [Time zones](../i18n/time-zones.md)).
A page that varies on a header has a different key from the one older releases made, and its first request after an upgrade is a miss (`docs/releases/6.1.txt`).

With no key it sets the flag true and returns `None`; so it does with no entry, once a `"HEAD"` has tried the key of an earlier `"HEAD"` (`django/middleware/cache.py:FetchFromCacheMiddleware.process_request`).
`UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response` returns the response untouched at the first of these that applies (`django/middleware/cache.py:UpdateCacheMiddleware.process_response`):

Its Cache-Control has `"private"`, `"no-cache"` or `"no-store"`, read in lower case by `split_directive_names`, so that `private="Set-Cookie"` counts too (`django/utils/http.py:split_directive_names`).

The middleware gives it to `patch_response_headers`, which adds `"Expires"` if absent and a `"max-age"`, keeping a smaller one already there ([Cache headers and conditional requests: `django/utils/cache.py`](http-caching.md)).

If the request has an `"Authorization"` header and the Cache-Control is not `"public"`, it adds Authorization to `"Vary"`, so each credential has its own page key, to simplify the keys, the documentation says (`docs/topics/cache.txt`).

A response with a callable `render` is stored by a post-render callback, which runs at once if it is rendered already; a template response refuses to be pickled before it is rendered (`django/template/response.py:SimpleTemplateResponse.__getstate__`).

`CacheMiddleware` subclasses both halves, and fetches on the way in and updates on the way out from one place in the list; the module's docstring keeps it for simple sites, the two halves being needed where another middleware "needs to affect the cache key", most often `LocaleMiddleware` (`django/middleware/cache.py`).

`CacheMiddleware.__init__` takes a cache timeout, a page timeout, and a key prefix and a cache alias as keyword arguments, and a comment separates a value provided as the default from one not provided: `key_prefix=None` gives the prefix `""`, `cache_alias=None` the alias `DEFAULT_CACHE_ALIAS`, `"default"`, and either left out keeps the setting's value (`django/middleware/cache.py:CacheMiddleware.__init__`).

`cache_page(timeout, *, cache=None, key_prefix=None)` calls `decorator_from_middleware_with_args(CacheMiddleware)` with `page_timeout=timeout` and always with the alias and the prefix (`django/views/decorators/cache.py:cache_page`).

So it runs inside the whole chain, after the URL is resolved, and returns a hit without `process_response` (`django/utils/decorators.py:make_middleware_decorator`; [A middleware as a decorator](../views/middleware-decorators.md)).
*The page cache's settings, with their defaults from `django/conf/global_settings.py`.*

`cache_page` stores the response before it passes back out through `MIDDLEWARE`, so a `"Vary"` that `SessionMiddleware` or `LocaleMiddleware` adds on the way out is not in the list it learns; the documentation keeps it for content safe to reuse for any request to the URL (`docs/topics/cache.txt`).
